Elated

/ih-LAY-tid/ - the stress falls on LAY · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Elated means overjoyed, thrilled.

Elated by the acceptance letter, Tomas read it aloud twice and taped it to the refrigerator at eye level.

Worked Example

When the examiner finally said 'passed,' Ren walked out of the DMV elated — grinning at strangers, calling everyone she had ever met, floating a full inch above the linoleum.

Elated is joy with lift in it — the word literally means carried up. It is stronger than pleased and sharper than happy: elation spikes, usually at one piece of good news, and you can feel it in the body — lightness, grinning, the urge to tell someone immediately.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

overjoyed: flooded with joy — the nearest plain twin

thrilled: joy with a jolt of excitement in it

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

crushed: flattened by disappointment

dejected: sunk low in spirits

Where it sits · how high the joy climbs — pleased → delighted → elated

pleased vs. elated: Pleased is quiet satisfaction — a nod and a small smile, several floors below elated.

delighted vs. elated: Delighted is real, sparkling happiness, but elated is stronger — joy with altitude, joy that wants to shout.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — e-

Prefix — e-: out, up (Latin ex-)

Root — lat

Root — lat: carried (Latin latus)

Suffix — -ed

Suffix — -ed: adjective ending: in that state

Put it together

Put it together: E- (up, out) + lat- (carried) + -ed = carried up. Latin latus, 'carried,' is a quiet workhorse root: relate carries a story back to its listeners, and elated describes you when good news carries you a foot off the ground.

Use the root in a new word: relate

Use the root in a new word: relate: Around the fire, the guide related the story of the valley's first winter.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral

Elated is for the spike of joy right after good news — results, wins, yeses. For durable good cheer use its unit-mates sanguine (settled optimism) or ebullient (overflowing spirits); elated is a moment, not a temperament. Its close kin exhilarated — in this unit's reference list — adds adrenaline to the joy.
